page.title: Backstage + GitHub — from service catalog to reviewed canon

sections.heading: Who owns what
sections.text: Backstage supplies service identity. Git holds the reviewed story. Source scans supply evidence; a human decides what it means.
bullets: **Read this as a guided tour:** choose Play or step forward. The page opens paused. Animation shows logical handoffs, not measured latency.

**Current implementation + company handoff:** the plugin, renderer and scanner exist here. Company authentication, repository access and hosted adapters are installation work; this page does not claim they are deployed.
**HLD and canon coexist:** preserve the design-document link. Canonical promotion is an explicit human review, never a consequence of being listed in Backstage.
**Confluence remains a viewer:** export compact JSON from the workbench and import a snapshot into Forge. Editing stays outside Confluence.

steps.text: Backstage supplies fully qualified service/API identities, ownership and endpoint links.
The editor uses those catalog choices; the narrative and its canonical status still require review.
The central Git repository holds authoritative specs, the registry, reviewed source pins and audit decisions.
GitHub Actions compares referenced source regions; it never executes watched service code.
A report gives the reviewer code differences and every affected diagram/step, without deciding behavioral impact.
A maintainer accepts a harmless change, records a regression, or reviews a deliberate spec update.
Published bindings automatically associate diagrams with Component and API pages in Backstage.

sections.heading: Author a service-bound story
sections.text: Use catalog identity for the actors and reviewed code anchors for the story beats. A proposed HLD stays linked to its design document.
bullets: **Company deployment boundary:** these flows describe the integration contract. Runnable read endpoints live in the development mock; the authenticated company backend and approved-Git provider must still be implemented and deployed.
**Identity:** bind `kind:namespace/name`, not a display name. Bind an API explicitly if its entity page should list the diagram.
**Source references:** pin a full immutable commit SHA, a repository path and unique literal start/end anchors. Line numbers help navigation; anchors define the watched region.
**Company backend:** supply authenticated context and proposal routes, actual reviewer identity and repository policy. The local portal simulates these decisions in its JSON store.
**Catalog limitations:** convert OpenAPI YAML and external references in the company API pipeline. A failed refresh must not silently remove saved bindings. Endpoint links do not invoke live APIs.

steps.text: The backend adapter paginates Component/API entities and maps owners, provided APIs, operations and endpoints.
Authenticated company context seeds the workbench with the catalog, spec and revision token.
Choose the service, API and operation; attach code references to stable step IDs. Preserve HLD provenance.
Submit the spec with its base revision. Stale proposals must be rejected instead of overwriting newer work.
The company adapter verifies the real reviewer and applies repository policy; a browser-supplied actor is not authorization.
An approved Git change becomes the published spec. Include it in the registry for source-drift scans.

sections.heading: Discover diagrams from a service
sections.text: A service page asks for diagrams bound to its exact entity identity. The backend derives associations from the approved specs this viewer may read.
bullets: **Company deployment boundary:** these flows describe the integration contract. Runnable read endpoints live in the development mock; the authenticated company backend and approved-Git provider must still be implemented and deployed.
**Automatic association:** inspect every section/tab for service bindings and explicit API bindings. Matching nodes also link to happy and alternate steps; a node without steps still associates.
**Freshness:** refresh every 60 seconds while visible, on focus and on demand. Cancel old requests when changing services. Approved additions/removals/rebindings update the next published snapshot.
**Access:** authenticate both the Backstage proxy and the central repository API. Cache by published revision and authorization scope; an all-diagram index must not leak to a restricted viewer.
**Empty is different from broken:** no matching diagrams returns an empty result; an unavailable/invalid index returns an error. Failed refreshes retain the last result and show a warning.

steps.text: The entity page reads its identity from Backstage useEntity and queries through the authenticated proxy.
The proxy allows GET requests and keeps its upstream token on the backend. Use identity forwarding for per-user visibility.
The company API obtains only published specs the requesting viewer is authorized to read.
Build associations from explicit service/API bindings. Match full references case-insensitively; namespaces and kinds remain distinct.
Return a versioned result with diagram cards, owners, HLD links, and matching happy/alternate step links.
The Diagrams tab displays the current result, including an explanatory empty state when no bindings match.
While visible, refresh every 60 seconds, on focus and on demand; switching services cancels stale requests.
If refresh fails, keep the last result and display a warning. Do not present an unavailable index as zero diagrams.

sections.heading: Scan source changes in GitHub
sections.text: A scheduled or manually dispatched workflow compares reviewed anchored source against current default-branch code. The result is evidence, not a behavioral verdict.
bullets: **Cadence:** weekdays at 08:23 America/New_York, including daylight-saving changes. GitHub scheduling can run late. Opt in with `FLOWVIEW_CANON_ENABLED=true` and configure `FLOWVIEW_REGISTRY`.
**Read and write identities:** a read-only source GitHub App token reads watched repositories; the central `GITHUB_TOKEN` writes review evidence. The runner uses one configured GitHub/GHES host.
**Stable comparison:** literal anchors follow code across unrelated line movement. Missing files, denied access or missing/duplicate/reversed anchors require repair.
**Deduplication and recovery:** reuse one review per changed reference scope, even if closed without a disposition. Reuse an interrupted run’s branch. Previously recorded regressions remain visible.
**Report-only mode:** manual `dry_run` saves Markdown/JSON evidence without opening PRs. Run summaries include clean scans and failures; report artifacts are retained for 30 days.

steps.text: Schedule or workflow dispatch starts a run against trusted default-branch tooling; never check out a report PR head.

log.text: Trusted default branch; watched code is data.

steps.text: Read the checked-in registry, registered specs, code reference pins and prior drift decisions.
Read immutable source blobs at the reviewed pin and the current source default-branch revision through the API.
Locate each unique literal anchor range and compare its text. Unrelated line movement alone is ignored.
Changed anchored text identifies every affected diagram and step. This still does not establish behavioral impact.

log.text: Source changed. Expected story and baseline remain unchanged.

steps.text: Create or reuse one evidence PR for the changed reference scope, plus Markdown/JSON reports and an Actions summary.

log.text: Review required. A closed report without a disposition is reused.

steps.text: If anchored content is unchanged, record a clean scan. No behavioral decision or baseline update is needed.
If source or anchors cannot be resolved, save repair evidence and fail the scan visibly; expected behavior stays unchanged.

log.text: Repair required; unreadable source is not a clean scan.

sections.heading: Choose the human disposition
sections.text: The same evidence can represent a harmless refactor, a regression, or an intended change. Only a human review supplies that interpretation.
bullets: **No impact:** label the report `flowview/no-impact` and close it. A validated decision advances only the exact reviewed source revision and records the audit decision.
**Regression:** label `flowview/regression`, include `Regression ticket: https://…` in the body and close. Preserve the expected story and code baseline while tracking the issue.
**Intentional change:** update the affected spec and reviewed pin in an ordinary reviewed PR. The author can be a human or agent; publication still follows repository review.
**No disposition:** simply closing or merging the evidence report leaves the baseline unchanged. The report is not an executable behavior update.

**Publication:** accepted pins and audit state are written atomically in one non-forced Git commit. If branch protection blocks bot writes, the company must route acceptance through its approved process.

steps.text: The maintainer reads the code diff and every affected diagram/step, then determines whether behavior changed.

log.text: Code drift is evidence, not a behavioral verdict.

steps.text: For a harmless change, the maintainer applies flowview/no-impact and closes the report.
The decision runner verifies the report, live actor permission, exact disposition and current evidence before accepting it.

log.text: Validate the decision against trusted current state.

steps.text: Commit the exact reviewed source pin and audit decision together. The expected narrative stays unchanged.

log.text: Reviewed pin + audit decision; never accept an unrelated later HEAD.

steps.text: For a regression, the maintainer links a real team issue, sets flowview/regression and closes the report.

log.text: Regression ticket linked; preserve the expected behavior.

steps.text: After validating the regression decision, write its audit state while retaining the expected story and accepted source pin.

log.text: Record regression; do not bless the broken behavior.

steps.text: For intended behavior, revise the spec and source pin in an ordinary PR; an agent may assist the author.

log.text: Proposed new expected behavior requires ordinary review.

steps.text: The reviewed spec update changes the approved story and pin together; the next published snapshot is discoverable.
Closing or merging a report with no disposition leaves the baseline unchanged. A later scan reuses that report.

log.text: No explicit disposition; no accepted revision.

sections.heading: Refuse an unsafe or stale decision
sections.text: A disposition is conditional on the evidence and repository state that were actually reviewed. A refused decision cannot advance canon.
bullets: **Gate inputs:** same-repository closed bot PR, expected branch and evidence marker, live write/maintain/admin actor permission, exactly one disposition, and a ticket for regression.

**Recheck evidence:** a changed scope or changed anchored source requires a rescan/review. No-impact acceptance pins the revision in the report even if unrelated later source commits leave that region unchanged.
**Races and policy:** a moved default branch or a blocked non-forced commit fails without accepting a baseline. Fix configuration or route through the company’s protected-branch process and rerun.
**Idempotence:** repeated identical decision events do not create another acceptance commit. Closed/labeled/edited events support adding a missing ticket and retrying.

steps.text: Load the live closed bot report and the event sender’s current repository permission from GitHub.
Validate report provenance, one explicit disposition and matching reviewed evidence. A regression also requires an issue.

report.detail: Expected bot PR and one disposition

steps.text: For no-impact acceptance, if the Git update is permitted, write the reviewed pin and audit atomically without forcing the branch. Regression records audit only and retains the previous pin.
If anchored source or report evidence changed, refuse acceptance and require a new scan and review.

evidence.detail: Source or evidence no longer matches

steps.text: An unprivileged actor, invalid report or ambiguous disposition is refused; the baseline remains untouched.
If branch policy or a concurrent default-branch update rejects the commit, fail the run and leave canon unchanged.

write.detail: Policy or concurrent update refused write

sections.heading: Compare runtime evidence to canon
sections.text: Source drift asks whether referenced code changed. Trace comparison asks how one observed execution differs from the approved story. Both feed reviewed proposals.
bullets: **Approve the reference:** paste/export Honeycomb JSON, sanitize it, map exact service/operation selectors, then explicitly review the mapping against the spec revision.
**Compare an incident:** preserve the unchanged prefix, branch at the first differing beat with independent step IDs, and keep canon untouched until a spec review accepts the overlay.

**Evidence boundaries:** a missing span is unknown. A received HTTP error still animates the observed call; only explicit delivery failure gets a broken edge. Queue buildup and backpressure require measured/explicit evidence.
**Do not invent the customer outcome:** later physical actions and phone UX require evidence/review. The baseline’s uninstrumented shared prefix is authored context, not newly verified behavior.

**Input and freshness:** one trace per import, up to 10,000 spans and 2 MB in the portal. Environment mismatches block comparison; changed selectors/budgets require reference reapproval. Bodies, headers and arbitrary attributes are dropped.

steps.text: Import exported trace JSON and retain only supported operational identity, timing and error attributes.
Match exact service/operation selectors; ambiguous or missing matches remain visible. Do not guess concurrency from timestamps.
Explicitly approve the sanitized reference mapping against the spec revision. Company integration applies real repository review policy.
Read the approved reference and authored expectations before comparing an incident trace.
Supply a new incident trace. Environment mismatches block comparison; missing measurements remain unknown.
Build an isolated alternate at the first differing beat. Preserve only the unchanged prefix and use independent divergent steps.
A human or agent may edit the alternate and propose it through normal spec review; comparison alone never changes canon.
